newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - OfficeMax, Staples/Office Depot.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - OfficeMax, Staples/Office Depot.

text.p: OfficeMax Inc said Wednesday it would buy 63 Staples and Office Depot superstores for $108.75 million. The deal is expected to be accretive to earnings.
A full text of the press release follows

CLEVELAND, March 12 /PRNewswire/ -- OfficeMax, Inc. (NYSE: OMX), the Cleveland-based office products superstore chain, today announced that it has reached an agreement in principle to acquire 63 Staples/Office Depot superstores in key major metropolitan markets where OfficeMax currently does not have a presence or is operating a limited number of stores. New market entries include Baltimore, Washington DC, San Diego, Tampa/St. Petersburg and Louisville, KY together with 14 stores in the Los Angeles area where OfficeMax entered the market this last year with 19 TriMax Super Centers. The Company also gained locations in 11 other markets.

OfficeMax's chief executive, Michael Feuer, said the Company has agreed to purchase the assets of 63 stores of Staples, Inc. (Nasdaq: SPLS) and Office Depot, Inc. (NYSE: ODP) for approximately $108.75 million in cash and anticipates that the acquisition will be accretive to earnings.

The transaction is subject to approval by the Federal Trade Commission and conditioned on the sale of the stores to OfficeMax being the predicate for a consent settlement of the Commissioners' investigation of the proposed merger between Staples and Office Depot.

OfficeMax currently operates 575 superstores in over 225 markets in 48 states, Puerto Rico and Mexico. In addition, the Company operates store-within-a-store modules of FurnitureMax and CopyMax, which are devoted exclusively to office furniture and "print-for-pay" services, respectively. The Company also operates OfficeMax OnLine on the Internet at http://www.officemax.com which enables individual consumers and businesses to buy a wide assortment of OfficeMax merchandise using their personal computers.

This release contains forward-looking statements which are subject to risk and uncertainties. OfficeMax's quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 27, 1996, contains additional discussion about these factors which could cause results to differ from Management's expectations.
